concerns.text: Task T002 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but declares a dependency on T001. A consumer cannot run before its producer, so the `[P]` tag is inaccurate.
Task T003 is tagged `[P]` yet depends on T002. This creates a consumer‑before‑producer ordering conflict for a task claimed to be parallel‑safe.
Task T004 is marked `[P]` but lists T003 as a prerequisite, violating the parallel‑safety guarantee.
Task T005 carries the `[P]` tag while depending on T004, which contradicts the claim of being safe to run in parallel.
Task T006 is `[P]` yet requires the output of T005, breaking the parallel‑safe contract.
Task T007 is labeled `[P]` but depends on T006, making it impossible to execute in parallel with its producer.
Task T009 is marked `[P]` but explicitly depends on *all* previous tasks, which is incompatible with a parallel‑safe designation.
